meta.description: Detect and adjust for horizontal pleiotropy in two-sample Mendelian randomization by distinguishing uncorrelated from correlated pleiotropy and selecting robust MR sensitivity methods.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: Fresh real-GWAS, synthetic-ground-truth, CAUSE, LCV, and MR-PRESSO outputs were retained as files; no result was fabricated.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 6 followed the shipped population-versus-individual boundary and declined a personal statin recommendation.

methodological_ground.detail: The planted CHP case reproduced an apparently significant IVW result with MR-PRESSO global p=0.9995, and the audit correctly escalated rather than treating it as causal.

code_usability.detail: All five shipped R examples parsed; fresh execution reached the exact CAUSE and MR-PRESSO example outputs and the SIMEX, LCV, RAPS, and sensitivity paths.

functional_suitability.note: The UHP/CHP decision flow, thresholds, alternatives, and explicit practice boundary cover the stated task.

reliability.note: The Common Errors material covers observed CAUSE, MR-PRESSO, LCV, and RAPS behavior; SIMEX itself does not set a seed.

performance_context.note: Progressive-disclosure references reduce entry-document load, although computationally intensive CAUSE and MR-PRESSO routes remain necessarily expensive.

agent_usability.note: The scenario decision tree, quantitative gates, error table, and explicit source-version checks are agent-actionable.

human_usability.note: Trigger language, scope limit, decision flow, and reporting checklist are readily discoverable.

security.note: No secrets, destructive operations, or raw command execution are present; data validation remains largely delegated to underlying R packages.

maintainability.note: Method-specific material is now split into six reference files and all referenced shipped files exist.

agent_specific.note: Precise triggering and cross-skill handoffs are strong; version-sensitive GitHub packages still require installation-time inspection.

recommendations.title: Seed the standalone SIMEX example
recommendations.problem: The standalone SIMEX script uses B=1000 stochastic refits without setting a seed.
recommendations.root_cause: The seed guidance is explicit for the sensitivity battery but not repeated in the separate SIMEX example.
recommendations.fix: Add a documented set.seed call before simex(), or accept a seed parameter and print it in the report.

recommendations.title: Label the CAUSE demo nuisance warning
recommendations.problem: The shipped CAUSE demo intentionally uses 50,000 variants and emits a package warning that fewer than 100,000 nuisance variants may be unstable.
recommendations.root_cause: The lightweight synthetic demonstration is smaller than CAUSE's nuisance-estimation recommendation.
recommendations.fix: Add one sentence beside the demo that its 50,000-variant size is pedagogic and real analyses should follow the package's larger-nuisance-variant guidance.
